parsed.explanation: Combined national/division regime poses high trans-visitor risk. Foreign passports/visas are screened against birth-sex definitions; mismatch can cause refusal, added evidence, fraud findings and detention. National/state orders restrict government-funded and some other facilities by birth sex; a bathroom arrest is documented and four states treat trespass. Custody assigns birth sex, with hormone denial, forced labour, solitary and sexual assault; a trans inmate failure-to-protect claim was dismissed. Minors face a care ban and school scrutiny. Partial protections and litigation do not neutralize enforced hostile rules.

entry_documents.exposure: Visa and entry screening can doubt sex if appearance, marker or records mismatch; X or nonbirth-marker passports may trigger refusal/advisory. Passports reported blocked; trans athletes barred. Material fraud can permanent ineligibility.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X passports remain valid; ACLU suit and legal-aid FAQ. Foreign passports are generally used, but visitor-facing remedy is limited.
entry_documents.interaction: Document discrepancy can move traveler into investigation, temporary detention, and birth-sex custody/facility rules.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: National/state custody assigns by birth sex; prison care withdrawal, hormone removal, solitary; immigration detention forced labour, beatings, severe sexual abuse; documented assault in men's prison and court dismissal.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: National hate-crime statute covers gender identity; pretrial release possible, but no effective custody remedy documented.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Bathroom arrest or visa questioning can lead to detention where placement, care denial, and sexual violence risk are severe.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: National order bars government-funded single-sex facilities; many state bans government buildings/schools and some private; division order supports bathroom/changing segregation; one arrest; four states criminalize refusal to depart.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Not all jurisdictions ban; some private settings and one city public-accommodation protections; no visitor-specific national exemption.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Use of public buildings, terminals, schools or emergency spaces may require checks, refusal, removal, arrest, then birth-sex custody.

care_services.exposure: Minor’s gender-affirming care banned in division and many states; institutional care/hormone denial documented; adult emergency/ward placement not documented but custody/immigration care abuse is.
care_services.protection: General medical care not documented as excluded for adult visitors; medication import not assessed; local crisis services reduced.
care_services.interaction: If illness, injury or detention reveals identity, hospital/ward or care placement may follow hostile facility rules; minors lack lawful care.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: State/national orders define sex by birth, frame trans presence as threat to women/children and ideology; counterterrorism documents mention radical gender ideology; school funding/prosecution threats.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Courts and some agencies still enforce national hate-crime/employment statutes; local advocacy and litigation.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Threat framing raises scrutiny, makes complaints harder, and increases chance institutional contact is hostile.

minors_guardians.exposure: Adult traveling with trans minor faces under-19 care ban, school athletics/facility restrictions, criminal investigation of schools/teachers, and records subpoenas; guardian may be treated as facilitating prohibited care.
minors_guardians.protection: Same-sex marriage/adoption recognition removes partner-status penalty; some city protections; no care exemption documented.
minors_guardians.interaction: Minor’s documents, sports, school activities, or health visits can out the child and trigger denial or investigation.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No trans-specific state violence rate; polls show majority support birth-sex documents/athletes; state hate-crime omits gender identity; safety varies by jurisdiction.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National hate-crime covers gender identity; one city ordinance; no documented organized street campaign in this division.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Assault may be charged under national law, but state silence and hostile policy may deter reporting or effective remedy.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Complaints over facility/border/custody often fail; Supreme Court allowed passport restrictions; state court dismissed trans prisoner claim; one city ordinance repealed.
remedies_unknowns.protection: ACLU lawsuit ongoing; equal-opportunity commissions and national housing/employment protections; litigation can block some orders.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Operative rules may shift; absence of evidence not safety; traveler-specific remedies not established.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar birth-sex facility rule and weak complaint remedy, but this regime adds border refusal/fraud risk, documented custody sexual assault, care denial for minors, and hostile state/national threat framing, so it rates lower than 0.35.

Comparable institutional exclusion and arrest/birth-sex custody. This case lacks an explicit universal emergency-care directive, but visa screening, immigration abuse, and a documented care ban for minors keep it near the 0.25 high-risk tier.

Below severe risk because there is no registry, checkpoint presentation offence, or near-automatic imprisonment for merely being trans. Engineered document screening and custody abuse still keep it far below 0.35 anchors.

parsed.synthesis: Hostile national document/entry screening, state facility restrictions, and birth-sex custody combine into a coherent high-risk operative regime. The passport mismatch is not merely paperwork: it can become denial, detention, fraud allegations and placement. Facility checks and arrests can channel a visitor into custody, where hormone denial, forced labour, solitary and sexual violence are documented. Minors face direct care denial. National anti-discrimination machinery, city protections and ongoing litigation exist, but they do not override enforced passport, facility or custody rules and sometimes validate them.
